card.title: Aufbau Principle, Pauli's Exclusion Principle, Hund's Rule and Electronic Configurations (up to Z = 30)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three rules build every ground-state configuration: **Aufbau** fills the lowest-energy orbital first (order 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p…, predicted by the (n + l) rule — hence K = [Ar] 4s¹, NEB 2023's example); **Pauli** caps each orbital at two opposite-spin electrons by forbidding any shared set of four quantum numbers; **Hund** fills degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing (N: 2p ↑ ↑ ↑).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - (n + l) rule: lower (n + l) fills first; tie → lower n - Capacity: orbital 2; subshell 2(2l + 1); shell 2n² - Cr: [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵; Cu: [Ar] 4s¹ 3d¹⁰ - Fe³⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵ (from Fe [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **4s before 3d — but also 4s out first:** filling order and removal order are different questions. Ions strip the highest-n shell first.  ·  **Pairing needs a partner orbital, not the same orbital:** Hund's rule forbids pairing while a degenerate orbital is still empty — O (2p⁴) pairs only because all three p orbitals already hold one electron.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "No two electrons in an atom can have identical values of all four quantum numbers." — Pauli; the reason matter occupies space at all.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***K (Z = 19) = [Ar] 4s¹*** — the (n + l) rule at work: 4s (4+0 = 4) beats 3d (3+2 = 5), so the 19th electron of potassium enters 4s, not 3d — the single clearest demonstration of Aufbau.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Filling Rules That Build the Periodic Table Quantum numbers give every electron an address; three rules decide the **order of occupation**: the **Aufbau principle** (fill lowest energy first), **Pauli's exclusion principle** (two electrons maximum per orbital, opposite spins) and **Hund's rule** (degenerate orbitals fill singly with parallel spins first).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Aufbau principle (building-up) Electrons occupy the **lowest-energy orbital available** before entering higher ones. Energy order (the diagonal rule): **1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d < 4p < 5s < 4d < 5p …** - The **(n + l) rule** predicts the order: lower (n + l) fills first; on a tie, lower n fills first. - 4s: n + l = 4 + 0 = 4 — fills **before** 3d: n + l = 3 + 2 = 5.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Diagonal chant: "1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p." (n + l) check for any disputed pair. Ions: "last in, first out" — strip the highest shell.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (3m): Explain Aufbau's principle with an example.** — Electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy, lowest first; the order follows the (n + l) rule (lower n + l first; tie → lower n): 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d < 4p.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): State Pauli's exclusion principle and one consequence.** — No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of all four quantum numbers. Consequence: an orbital holds at most two electrons with opposite spins (↑↓); shell capacity is 2n².

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Write configurations in full for Z ≤ 18; core notation [Ar] is fine beyond. For ions, show the neutral configuration first, then strike out — the marking scheme follows the steps.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **(n + l) rule** — the quick ordering tool: sum n and l; lower sum fills first; equal sums → lower n first. It reproduces the whole diagonal order without memorising it.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Aufbau: fill lowest energy first — order 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s…, predicted by (n + l), tie → lower n. Pauli: no two electrons share all four quantum numbers → orbital max 2, ↑↓. Hund: degenerate orbitals fill singly with parallel spins before pairing.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The periodic table's block structure is the Aufbau order made visible: s-block (groups 1–2), p-block (13–18), d-block (3–12), f-block — the filling sequence *is* the table's shape.

rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Aufbau principle** | Electrons fill the lowest-energy orbitals first | 4s fills before 3d | | **Pauli exclusion principle** | No two electrons share all four quantum numbers | Orbital capacity = 2 | | **Hund's rule** | Degenerate orbitals fill singly with parallel spins before pairing | N:…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 NEB 2023 (3m, verified PYQ) — Explain Aufbau's principle with an example **Statement:** electrons enter the orbital of lowest energy first; higher orbitals are occupied only after all lower ones are filled. The energy order follows the (n + l) rule — lower (n + l) first, and on a tie the lower n first.…  ·  ### Deep dive — the three filling rules and where each one bites - **Aufbau** — fill subshells in order of increasing n + l; for ties, lower n wins. Hence 4s (n+l = 4) fills before 3d (n+l = 5), and the familiar order 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p 6s 4f 5d 6p follows. Remember that after filling, 4s electrons are *removed first* when cations form (Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶, not 3d⁴4s²).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Comparison Tables **The three rules side by side** | Rule | Statement | Governs | Visible effect | |---|---|---|---| | **Aufbau** | Lowest energy orbital fills first | Order of subshells | 4s before 3d; K = [Ar] 4s¹ | | **Pauli** | All four quantum numbers cannot repeat | Capacity | Orbital = 2 electrons, ↑↓ | |…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Ionisation order vs filling order:** electrons are **removed from the outermost shell** — Fe²⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁶, not [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴. 4s fills first but also empties first.  ·  **Hund's rule scope:** it applies **only within a degenerate set** (p³, d⁵…); it never overrides Aufbau's energy ordering across different subshells.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Exceptions are ground-state facts:** Cr and Cu configurations apply to the neutral ground-state atoms; their ions follow the normal removal order (Cu⁺ = 3d¹⁰).  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Write the configuration of Fe (Z = 26) and of Fe³⁺; why is Fe³⁺ more stable than Fe²⁺?** — Fe: [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶; Fe³⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵ (4s² removed first, then one 3d). rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): State Hund's rule and illustrate with nitrogen.** — Degenerate orbitals are occupied singly with parallel spins before any pairing. N (Z = 7): 1s² 2s² 2p³ → the three 2p electrons sit in three separate p orbitals as ↑ ↑ ↑.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Predict the ground-state configuration of Cr (Z = 24) and explain the anomaly.** — [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵ instead of [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴: the half-filled 3d⁵ gains maximum exchange energy, and promoting one 4s electron to 3d costs little because 4s and 3d are nearly degenerate.
